notes: Bands follow SAG-AFTRA low budget agreement tiers, which is what makes them meaningful rather than arbitrary round numbers: each band is the point at which the cost structure of a production genuinely changes. Scope parameters translate each band into the narrative bounds a line producer applies intuitively.

items.label: Micro budget
items.guild_context: SAG-AFTRA Ultra Low Budget Agreement equivalent; deferred compensation, skeleton crew, no guild minimums at standard rates
items.rationale: At this level the production has no money to move. Every location change costs a shooting day in load-in and travel that the schedule does not have, every named speaking role is a paid performer and a callsheet line, and period costuming and set dressing are simply unaffordable. Tension must be generated by what characters say and withhold, not by what is staged. Narrative economy is high because there is no budget for a scene that performs only one story function.
citations: SAG-AFTRA Ultra Low Budget Agreement tier documentation
Saturation.io (2024), Feature Film Budget Template and How to Create a Film Budget
Medium / The Film & Script Desk, De Bortoli, L. (January 2025), Write Big on a Small Budget: 8 Essential Tips for Low-Budget Screenwriting

items.label: Low budget independent
items.guild_context: SAG-AFTRA Modified Low Budget Agreement; reduced guild minimums, small but professional crew
items.rationale: A real if modest schedule becomes possible: a supporting ensemble, a handful of distinct environments, and practical effects done in camera. Recent-period settings within roughly thirty years are affordable because costume and vehicle dressing can be sourced rather than built. Digital effects remain out of reach because they carry post-production cost that this band cannot absorb.
citations: SAG-AFTRA Modified Low Budget Agreement tier documentation
Tools for Film (2026), How to Build a Realistic Indie Film Budget: A Line-by-Line Breakdown
Saturation.io (2024), Feature Film Budget Template and How to Create a Film Budget

items.label: Mid-range independent
items.guild_context: Full guild agreements; DGA and SAG-AFTRA standard terms, full department heads
items.rationale: Full guild terms and complete departments support an ensemble cast, location moves as a normal part of the schedule, and one or two staged set pieces. Any historical period becomes possible where the budget is deliberately allocated to it, which is a trade against other departments rather than a free choice. Digital effects are available but bounded: augmentation and clean-up, not sustained creature or environment work.
citations: DGA 2024-2025 Low Budget Agreement rate documentation
Tools for Film (2026), How to Build a Realistic Indie Film Budget: A Line-by-Line Breakdown
Saturation.io (2024), Feature Film Budget Template and How to Create a Film Budget

items.label: Studio
items.guild_context: Full guild agreements at studio scale; typical studio features increasingly sit at twenty million and above
items.rationale: Scope stops being the binding constraint and genre convention takes over. Null bounds mean the budget imposes no ceiling this system should enforce; large ensembles, international location shooting and extensive practical and digital effects are all supportable. Conflicts at this tier come from rating and territory, not from money.
citations: Saturation.io (2024), Feature Film Budget Template and How to Create a Film Budget
Tools for Film (2026), How to Build a Realistic Indie Film Budget: A Line-by-Line Breakdown
